features.feature_value: Profanity/insults led to removal for both versions.
features.evidence_span: If there was profanity, or insults.  Both got flagged as being removed.
features.rationale: The participant explicitly states profanity/insults were the basis for deciding removal.

features.feature_value: They would allow most content but reject extreme language/hate speech or inappropriate targeting of children.
features.evidence_span: I would allow pretty much anything except for extreme language or things that could be considered hate speech against someone. Or anything inappropriately targeting children.
features.rationale: They describe clear exception criteria tied to hate speech and child-targeting.

features.feature_value: Language was judged for hate-baiting and fear-mongering; those cues drove the decision.
features.evidence_span: based on the language in them and whether or not they were hate baiting and fear mongering.
features.rationale: The participant names specific content cues (hate baiting, fear mongering) as decision drivers.

features.feature_value: They weighed whether posts were honest/debate-oriented; inflammatory/curse-word lists were rejected.
features.evidence_span: considered whether these posts were written in the spirit of honest expression and debate... language being used. Lists with curse words or inflammatory language were out.
features.rationale: Their criteria combine an intent/spirit assessment with language-level filtering.

features.feature_value: Decision relied on language, arguments presented, and overall tone.
features.rationale: They directly list the textual dimensions used to judge the posts.

features.feature_value: They look for substance for healthy conversation; profanity/rhetoric leads to rejection, and mirror-image reasoning suggests common ground.
features.evidence_span: I look for some substance that could spark healthy conversation... If the messages were mostly rhetoric or contained profanity, I rejected... how the reasoning could be created into "mirror images"... we should be able to find some common ground.
features.rationale: The participant emphasizes substance and mirror-image reasoning as part of how the pair influences their judgments.

features.feature_value: They tried to set feelings aside and allow equal time to the opposing side.
features.evidence_span: had to distance myself from feelings... have to contemplate and allow equal time to the opposing side
features.rationale: Their stated process reflects affect regulation and a balance principle.

features.feature_value: Freedom of speech accepted unless inciting/encouraging violence; removals were based on being difficult to understand or seeming to incite violence.
features.evidence_span: as long as it isn't inciting or encouraging violence... difficult to understand or I felt may incite someone to violence.
features.rationale: They articulate a speech-permissiveness rule with an exception tied to violence incitement.
